name: Nebraska
nameStory: From an Otoe and Omaha phrase meaning 'flat water,' describing the Platte River. Pioneers put it more bluntly: the Platte is a mile wide and an inch deep, too thick to drink and too thin to plow.
capitalStory: The town was called Lancaster until 1867, when opponents of moving the capital there renamed it Lincoln - betting that legislators with Southern sympathies would refuse to put their government in a town named after the recently assassinated president. The gambit failed completely and the name stuck.

majorFeatures.name: Platte River
majorFeatures.note: The natural highway of the Oregon Trail

majorFeatures.name: Sandhills
majorFeatures.note: Grass-covered dunes over a quarter of the state

majorFeatures.name: Chimney Rock
majorFeatures.note: The most recorded landmark on the Oregon Trail

funFacts: Nebraska is the only state with a one-house legislature, and its members run without party labels.
The Sandhills are the largest sand dune field in the Western Hemisphere - they only look like grassland because grass has pinned them in place.
Beneath them sits part of the Ogallala Aquifer, the groundwater that irrigates much of the Great Plains.
Hundreds of thousands of settlers followed the Platte west; wagon ruts are still visible in the rock.
